h34s `NEXT_VERSION`. This placeholder collects notes for the next release while the work lands. The version is not decided yet.

## Breaking changes

<!-- claude 2026-10-20: created: streams are sent with Response.sendStream (ADR-0004) and the test helpers (ADR-0006); it reverses two statements of the 0.2.0-alpha.1 notes -->
- **Streams are sent, not returned.** A handler streams with `Response.sendStream(stream)`, in Kyo and in ZIO, and returns the `Sent` value that it gives. A handler that returns a `kyo.Stream` or a `ZStream` no longer compiles; the compiler message names `Response.sendStream(stream)`. This reverses the `0.2.0-alpha.1` notes, where `sendStream` became a returned stream of strings; there is no `ZHandler.sendStream` (`0.1.0-alpha.1` had one with another signature). `sendStream` writes the head when you call it and, over a socket, flushes it at once, so clients get the status and headers before the first element. After the call the status is fixed: a stream failure, also before the first element, closes the connection, and the `sendStream` step fails with the stream's error, so your program, a scope or a transaction around it can roll back. The server logs the failure once. A stream over Nitro's in-process local fetch, for example a server-side `$fetch` to your own route, now streams head-first; the `0.2.0-alpha.1` notes said it was rejected with an opaque 500. `HandlerEffects` gains `Env[Fetch & HandlerTransport]` and `HandlerEnv` gains `HandlerTransport`, which h34s provides. Test handler functions with the new `KHandler.test` and `ZHandler.test`, which give a `TestResponse` with the head and the body; the manual provisioning with `Var.runTuple` or `ZIO.stateful` no longer compiles. See the [migration guide](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/content/2.reference/4.migration.md#send-streams-with-responsesendstream).

<!-- claude 2026-10-19: created: the strict JSON content type default (issue #41); changed: requests without a body are not affected (review) -->
- **JSON reads require a content type.** `HandlerOptions.requireJsonContentType` now defaults to `true`, so `request.body.json[A]` answers 415 for a request that has a body but no `Content-Type`. A request without a body is not affected. Browsers send some cross-site requests without a content type and without a CORS preflight; the new default keeps them away from JSON reads without any setup. `$fetch` with an object body and `curl --json` already send `application/json`. To keep the old behavior for one handler, pass `HandlerOptions(requireJsonContentType = false)`. `Request.fake` follows the same default and takes the same parameter. See the [migration guide](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/content/2.reference/4.migration.md#json-reads-require-a-content-type). <!-- claude 2026-10-20: changed: the migration guide's new path (issue #25) -->

<!-- claude 2026-10-19: created: ZIO follows Kyo on finalizer failures (issue #40); changed: streaming-before-return and disconnect logging (review) -->
- **A dying ZIO finalizer keeps the response.** The ZIO adapter now behaves like the Kyo core: a request-scope finalizer that dies is logged on the server as `h34s: a ZIO finalizer failed`, with `Cause.prettyPrint`, and the client gets the value, the `Unit` response or the safe error that the program produced. Before, it turned that response into an opaque 500. This also applies to a streaming handler, before and after it calls `Response.sendStream`. Streamed bodies already behaved this way. A finalizer that dies during a client disconnect is now logged too. <!-- claude 2026-10-20: changed: streaming handlers call Response.sendStream (ADR-0004) --> Move cleanup that must succeed for the response to be correct into the program. See the [migration guide](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/content/2.reference/4.migration.md#a-dying-zio-finalizer-keeps-the-response). <!-- claude 2026-10-20: changed: the migration guide's new path (issue #25) -->

## Verified since `0.2.0-alpha.1`

- **PostgreSQL 16.** The ZIO demo's Skunk Notes routes ran in a production build against PostgreSQL 16.15 with `scram-sha-256` authentication. `POST /api/notes` answered 201, invalid input answered 422, and `GET /api/notes` listed the note. Skunk's SCRAM login worked in the bundle. After `SIGTERM`, the server exited with status 0 and no session stayed open. See the [compatibility matrix](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/content/2.reference/3.compatibility.md#locally-verified-in-a-cloud-session-2026-10-19). <!-- claude 2026-10-20: changed: the compatibility page's new path (issue #25) -->
- **kyo-sql.** The kyo-sql code in the [database guide](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/content/1.guide/08.database.md#run-the-kyo-sql-tests) ran against PostgreSQL 16 in Node: insert and list, a unique violation mapped to a `SafeError`, two rollbacks, and a nested transaction that rolls back only its own part. A new opt-in suite, `KyoSqlPostgresSuite`, runs it when `H34S_POSTGRES_URL` is set. It has not run inside a Nitro bundle. <!-- claude 2026-10-20: changed: the database guide's new path (issue #25) -->
- **Build memory.** The cause of the demo's large build heap is now measured. Nitro bundles the linked Scala.js twice in one process: once for the prerendered Nuxt Content route and once for the server, with source maps. Without the new `scalaPrerender: 'stub'` option, the demo's `nuxt build` needs more than 4 GiB of heap (6144 MiB passed in one run). With it, a 4096 MiB heap limit passed. The scripts keep `--max-old-space-size=8192`. See the [development guide](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/development.md#production-build). <!-- claude 2026-10-19: created: the result with scalaPrerender: 'stub' -->

## Changes

<!-- claude 2026-10-20: created: the server-side $fetch returns in both runtimes (ADR-0005, ADR-0006) -->
- **The server-side `$fetch` returns, in Kyo and in ZIO.** `KHandler.$fetch` and `ZHandler.$fetch` call another route of your app, Scala or JavaScript, with the verbs `raw`, `text`, `as`, `get` and `post`. A path that starts with `/` is answered in-process by Nitro, with your `app.baseURL` in front, as Nuxt's `$fetch` does, and with the incoming cookies and `authorization`; an absolute URL gets only the headers that you pass. The called route sees only the `_platform` and `waitUntil` entries of your request's `event.context`. `raw` returns at the head: `FetchResponse.Plain`, or `FetchResponse.Streamed` for a response that `Response.sendStream` sent or that has a stream content type. A streamed body is a Kyo `Stream[String, Async & Scope & Abort[FetchError]]` or a `ZStream[Any, FetchError, String]`, and a body that breaks after its head fails with `FetchError.BodyFailed`. A body that you do not read to its end is cancelled when your scope closes, and the cancel waits for the called route's cleanup. Statuses do not throw and nothing retries: `text`, `as`, `get` and `post` fail with `FetchError.Status` unless the status is 2xx. `get` decodes the JSON as it arrives, so model the `{"data": ...}` envelope of an h34s route. `headerValues(name)` keeps each `set-cookie` apart. `HandlerEnv` gains `Fetch`, which h34s provides, and `ZHandler.test(handler)(request, fetch)` answers calls in tests with `Fetch.fake`, as `KHandler.test` does. See [Kyo handlers](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/content/1.guide/03.kyo.md#call-other-routes-with-fetch), [ZIO handlers](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/content/1.guide/04.zio.md#call-other-routes-with-fetch) and the [migration guide](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/content/2.reference/4.migration.md#call-other-routes-with-fetch).

- **PostgreSQL in CI.** A new `postgres` job in the Scala.js libraries workflow runs PostgreSQL 16 with SCRAM, the kyo-sql suite, the demo's production build, `smoke.mjs` and a `SIGTERM` session check. It runs on pull requests and pushes to `main` that touch the libraries or the example; it does not run on release tags. Its first run failed on a wrong session count; the [corrected job](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/actions/runs/39277276171/job/118144813255) passed on pull request #45.
- **`scalaPrerender: 'stub'`.** The Nuxt module `@yuri4n/h34s-nuxt` has a new option. With `'stub'`, a production build keeps the linked Scala.js out of Nitro's prerender bundle, so a build that prerenders routes bundles the Scala.js once. While Nuxt prerenders, every Scala.js route answers 501; the server output does not change. If a prerendered page calls a Scala.js route anyway, h34s logs the request, and the build stops after prerendering with a list of those requests, because a page that catches the 501, as `useFetch` does, would be saved with its error state. The default, `'bundle'`, keeps the earlier behavior, and other values are a `TypeError`. The demo uses the option: its prerendering took 3.6 to 3.9 seconds instead of 47 to 59, and its build passed with a 4096 MiB heap limit. `@yuri4n/h34s-nuxt/rollup` also exports the plugin, `scalaPrerenderStub`. The packed-module check (`pnpm test:package`) builds a Nuxt application with the option. The option ships with the next `@yuri4n/h34s-nuxt` release. See [npm tooling](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/content/1.guide/13.npm-tooling.md#keep-scalajs-out-of-the-prerender-bundle). <!-- claude 2026-10-19: created: the scalaPrerender option (issue #30), its build error and its real-build check (review F1, F2); a third build's time (review F7) --> <!-- claude 2026-10-20: changed: the npm tooling guide's new path (issue #25) -->

<!-- claude 2026-10-20: created: named model types (issue #66, ADR-0014) -->
- **Named model types.** Your Scala models now have names in the generated TypeScript. `h34s-scala` writes `h34s-models.d.ts` into each Scala.js output, with one `export type` per model that a route returns, and each route declaration refers to the models by name. The h34s Nuxt module maps `#h34s/models` to them, so your app writes `import type { NoteView } from '#h34s/models'` and `useAsyncData<NoteView[]>(...)` with no hand-written interface. Both schema bridges name their records after the Scala type, and the Kyo bridge also names sealed traits and enums. A hand-written converter names its type with the new `WireType.Named`. A generic instantiation such as `Page[Note]` is written out where it is used. Two Scala types with one TypeScript name and different structures stop `h34s-scala` with a message that names both types and their routes. Only response models are named; request-body models follow with the typed route registry. A `match` over `WireType` in your own code needs a `Named` case. See [use the models in your app](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/content/1.guide/02.routes.md#use-the-models-in-your-app) and [ADR-0014](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/design/adr/0014-named-model-types.md).

## Alpha limits

- kyo-sql inside a Nitro bundle and other Nitro presets remain unverified.
- The demo's production build needs more than 4 GiB of Node heap without `scalaPrerender: 'stub'`. With the stub (measured with an equivalent temporary hook), it still needs more than Node's 2240 MiB default on a 15.7 GiB cloud VM. Its scripts pass 8 GiB. <!-- claude 2026-10-19: created: the limit with the stub; the 2240 MiB run used a temporary hook (review F3) -->
